question: Should any protected internal-context marker found in an opaque `channelData` key or value cause the entire `channelData` object to be discarded before dispatch?
rationale: This is an intentional security-versus-delivery compatibility choice: whole-object deletion is conservatively fail-closed, but it can suppress otherwise valid provider payloads and cannot be settled by tests alone without owner intent.

options.title: Approve whole-object suppression
options.body: Treat any protected fragment in opaque channelData as taint for the complete provider payload, then require exact-head safe/rejected live proof before merge.

options.title: Remove only tainted leaves
options.body: Preserve unaffected channelData branches, but require provider-shape validation proving that partial mutation cannot create malformed or misleading native payloads.

options.title: Split parsing from security policy
options.body: Land stringified channelData parsing separately and pause the new suppression behavior until the permanent opaque-payload contract is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve whole-object suppression
recommendation.body: Treat any protected fragment in opaque channelData as taint for the complete provider payload, then require exact-head safe/rejected live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history most directly covers shared channelData and interactive outbound delivery semantics.
